requirement: Habeas MUST bundle a `habeas` skill whose description tells agents to use it at the start of any work in a Habeas project, naming as signs of one a `habeas` dev-dependency, a `habeas.toml`, `{req}` directives in the book, and `{impl}`, `{test}`, or `{cite}` references in code.
rationale:
The requirement has one obligation: Habeas must bundle a `habeas` skill whose description tells agents to use it at the start of any work in a Habeas project. The description must name four signs of such a project.

**Implementation.** `assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md` carries the `{impl}` reference, via an `:impl:` anchor on the requirement, and is the bundled skill.
- Its front-matter `description` begins "Use at the start of any work in a project that tracks requirements with Habeas".
- It then names all four signs: "a `habeas` dev-dependency", "a `habeas.toml`", "`{req}` directives in its mdBook", and "`{impl}`/`{test}`/`{cite}` references in code".
- The skill sits under `assets/skills`, the directory the `Cargo.toml` `package.metadata.symposium.skills` entry (`source.path = "assets/skills"`) points to. That is the bundling mechanism. It carries an `{impl}` reference to `requirements.integration.symposium`, not to this subject, so I did not assess it here.

**Test.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_habeas_skill_is_used_at_the_start_of_any_work_in_a_habeas_project]` carries the `{test}` reference. It reads the bundled skill's description through the `description("habeas")` helper. It asserts the "Use at the start of any work…" opening and that each of the four signs appears. That covers every part of the obligation.

**Unspecified behavior.** I found none.
